candidate.selection_reason: Defines core parsing regex changed from /\S/ to /\S+/g -> affects all string parsing operations throughout jQuery
candidate.source_summary: core_rnotwhite is a core utility regex used throughout jQuery for splitting strings on whitespace. It processes various inputs including data types, class names, event types, and callback options.
candidate.sink_summary: The regex output is used in multiple security-sensitive contexts: AJAX data type processing, DOM class manipulation, event handling, and callback configuration - all of which can affect security controls and parsing behavior.
candidate.guard_summary: No specific validation guards on the regex itself. The change from /\S/ to /\S+/g affects how whitespace-separated values are tokenized throughout the entire library.
candidate.risk_pattern: Global regex change from single non-whitespace character matching to greedy non-whitespace sequence matching affects all string splitting operations, potentially altering parsing behavior for space-separated values in security-sensitive contexts.
enclosing_conditions: String processing in AJAX data types
candidate.context_summary: Core utility regex used throughout jQuery for splitting strings on whitespace. Affects AJAX data type parsing, DOM class manipulation, event handling, and callback options processing. The change from single-character to greedy matching alters tokenization behavior.

target_cwe.description: User input should not be used in regular expressions without first being escaped, otherwise a malicious user may be able to inject an expression that could require exponential time on certain inputs.
patterns: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
remediation_steps: Implement resource consumption limits, rate limiting, and proper cleanup mechanisms for all operations.
